subject: MaplePay: sudden p99 & error spike after model v2.1 + q4_0 rollout
messages:

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-17T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Alert — MaplePay p99 up after v2.1/q4_0 rollout

Quick heads-up: monitoring flagged a jump in MaplePay's p99 latency from ~220ms to ~870ms around 2027-04-17T15:05Z after the v2.1 model + q4_0 quant profile rolled in. Error rate for their token-generation route also climbed from 0.2% -> 1.9%. Throughput appears reduced by ~28% under baseline traffic.

I pulled a sample trace and attached the p99 graph + an error sample (maplepay_error_sample.json). Customer on a dedicated pool with pinned variant v2.1-q4_0. They're hitting SLOs now.

Asking for triage: can someone from runtime take a look at kernel/latency changes and whether this profile introduced unexpected stalling? If it's an accuracy regression as well, we'll need a rollback plan.

- Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Apr 17, 2027 at 6:00 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Dylan: please prioritize kernel trace and scheduler logs around 2027-04-17T15:00–15:30Z.

Quick update from runtime triage:
- Confirmed increased kernel scheduler wait times correlated with q4_0's smaller GEMM tiling leading to higher per-token CPU sync overhead on some AVX2 host paths. Under MaplePay's request patterns (many short sessions with low prefix cache reuse) the execution never hit efficient batching thresholds, so quantization overhead dominated.
- We also observed elevated tokenization failures (UTF-8 edge cases) for ~0.4% of requests — linked to a new fast-path that assumed normalized input; fallback path raised error rate.
- Attached a short trace snippet and a suggested patch to disable the fast normalize path for the affected route.

Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Monica to roll back to v2.0-q8_0 (already in progress). Expect p99 recovery within ~20–40 minutes after traffic shifts.
2) We will publish a revised q4_0 profile v2.1-q4_0.1 that tweaks tiling and disables the fast-normalize shortcut for safety.
3) Postmortem + canary strategy: run q4_0 family in isolated canary with synthetic short-session load for 48 hours before broad promotion.

I'll open a runtime ticket with traces: INF-4521.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: MaplePay — rollback complete; initial findings and next steps

Elena / Marcus — quick status update now that Monica has completed the rollback to v2.0-q8_0 (timestamp: 2027-04-18T09:12Z):

What happened:
- Root cause appears to be an interaction between the new q4_0 quantization tiling and MaplePay's traffic profile (many short, low-cache-reuse sessions). That combination increased CPU sync overhead and raised p99 and error rates. A fast-path for input normalization also surfaced tokenization edge-case errors.

Impact:
- Peak p99 observed ~870ms (baseline ~220ms). Error rate peaked ~1.9% but is now back to baseline after rollback. Throughput delta ~-28% under same load.

What we did:
- Rolled back to v2.0-q8_0 (completed). Recovery observed within ~25 minutes of rollback start.
- Runtime will publish a patched q4_0 profile (v2.1-q4_0.1) with tiling adjustments and fast-normalize disabled.
- We'll run an extended canary with short-session synthetic traffic targeting MaplePay-like patterns before re-promoting.

Next steps / asks:
- We will share a postmortem and the canary schedule within 24 hours.
- Action for MaplePay: if you can share a representative sample of short-session prompts (anonymized), it will help validate the revised profile faster.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with executive priority and will follow up with a concise RCA for Marcus.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
